name: Engage Marin 101 — quiz
abstract: Ten questions to check what you learned about Engage Marin.
courseDescription: Notes, slides, and a quiz about using Engage Marin to invite community ideas, learn what matters, and share what happens next.

grades.name: A
grades.message: Excellent. You can explain how to run an engagement and ask the right questions.

grades.name: B
grades.message: Strong work. Keep asking how you will use the feedback and tell people what you learned.

grades.name: C
grades.message: A sound start. Read the explanations, then check the notes for the ones you missed.

grades.name: D
grades.message: Go back to the key terms and the do’s and don’ts in the notes, then try again.

grades.name: F
grades.message: Start with the notes. Then take the quiz again.

questions.text: Which is a reason to ask residents for input?

options.text: You can decide the result before people share.
You reach more people and hear different views.
You keep every idea inside the County team.
You avoid hearing from people who disagree.

questions.hint: Think about who you hear from.
questions.explanation: Why it matters says you reach more people and hear different views.

questions.text: What can happen when an engagement ends with no word on what happened?

options.text: The question opens again by itself.
Partners lose their links.
The platform deletes every idea.
People share ideas and never learn what happened.

questions.hint: Think about what people want to hear back.
questions.explanation: The Problem section says some people share ideas and never learn what happened.

questions.text: What does the Solution say to do first?

options.text: Publish a campaign right away.
Ask three questions about what to learn, who to hear from, and how to use feedback.
Write the final recap.
Choose the title of the welcome video.

questions.explanation: The Solution section starts with three questions: what you want to learn, who you want to hear from, and how you will use their feedback.

options.text: A group of ideas about one topic.
A post that shares progress.
Several related questions brought together under one larger effort.
A page with background on a question.

questions.explanation: Key terms defines a campaign as several related questions brought together under one larger effort.

questions.text: A theme is a group of related ideas that helps you see what people are saying.
questions.explanation: Key terms defines a theme as a group of related ideas that helps you see what people are saying across many responses.

questions.text: What does closing the loop mean?

options.text: Telling people what you heard, what you learned, and what happens next.
Ending a question so no one can read it.
Turning off partner links.
Sending one more reminder to join.

questions.hint: It is about telling people what happened.
questions.explanation: Key terms defines closing the loop as telling people what you heard, what you learned, and what happens next.

questions.text: Which is a Do when you write a question?

options.text: Use internal project names.
Lead people toward a preferred answer.
Ask one short, open question.
Invite partners after you publish.

questions.explanation: Do’s and don’ts says to ask one short, open question.

questions.text: A good invitation focuses on the County, not on the people taking part.
questions.hint: Think about who the invitation is for.
questions.explanation: Do’s and don’ts says to focus on what people want to share, not to write about the County instead of the people taking part.

questions.text: Which is one of the first questions to ask?

options.text: Which video format should we use?
What color should our logo be?
How will we use their feedback?
Who will write the About page?

questions.hint: It is about what happens to the feedback.
questions.explanation: Questions to ask includes how you will use their feedback.

questions.text: Which statement belongs on the checklist?

options.text: We will wait to share what we learned.
We will invite partners after we launch.
We have written the answer before asking the question.
Someone will monitor activity and post updates.

questions.hint: Someone has to follow the conversation.
questions.explanation: The Checklist says someone will monitor activity and post updates.
